bullets.title: Semis posted worst 2-day momentum crash ever; bounce underway but bar is high into earnings
bullets.body: The Tech Momentum index posted back-to-back 10% down days for the first time ever, with the SOX down ~15-28% from June 22 highs. High-beta momentum tech suffered its worst two-day decline since Covid (-18%) driven by crowding, low liquidity, and quarter-end rebalancing — GS notes record net short selling in US Tech, particularly semis and hardware. Futures are bouncing Monday (+0.46% S&P, +1.2% Nasdaq) but SOX is up 88% YTD vs SPX +14%, creating a high bar for earnings execution.

bullets.title: NVDA Kyber platform delayed to 2028 on PCB manufacturing snags; AMD/Google get a window
bullets.body: NVDA's next-gen Kyber NVL144 rack-scale architecture for Rubin Ultra chips has been pushed back 12+ months to 2028 due to PCB midplane manufacturability challenges, per SemiAnalysis. JPM sees this creating a competitive opening for AMD and Google at the high-performance AI tier; AVGO's 85% HBM fulfillment vs NVDA's stronger HBM access has shifted NVDA ahead of AVGO as top mega-cap compute idea.

bullets.title: DRAM is now the binding AI supply constraint; ASP trajectory sharply higher through 2026
bullets.body: Citi revised 2026 DRAM ASP growth to +44%/+20%/+13% QoQ for 2Q/3Q/4Q (vs prior +37%/+13%/+11%), as AI CPU demand replaces CoWoS as the gating factor. JPM notes semis revenue hit $131.9B in May (+119% YoY, +34% ex-memory), with Samsung expected to report ~18x YoY Q2 operating profit on Tuesday. ABF substrate availability is increasingly constraining, with CoWoS capacity no longer a reliable supply proxy.

bullets.title: META's cloud capacity monetization plan sparks sector de-rating but hyperscalers favored over semis
bullets.body: META's announcement of plans to sell excess AI compute capacity triggered the sector-wide semis selloff, but multiple desks frame this as a valuation play rather than demand destruction — META remains compute-constrained and the four high-margin use cases support continued 2027 capex surge. MS's Wilson and Morgan Stanley strategy both pivot to favoring hyperscalers over semiconductors; CRWV/NBIS backlog exposure to META (36-45%) flagged as manageable since META is monetizing older-gen GPUs, not cannibalizing next-gen contracts.

bullets.title: TSMC raises 2027-28 capex to $75-80bn; gross margins lifted to 66.9-67.3%
bullets.body: TSMC is accelerating N3/N2 and CoWoS capacity, targeting 200kwpm/130kwpm by end-2027. Citi raises 2027/2028 estimates +13%/+21% with a new NT$3,800 target; Morgan Stanley lifts WFE forecasts to $155bn/+$202bn/$227bn for 2026/2027/2028. TSMC 2026 capex unchanged at $55bn.

bullets.title: June payrolls disappoint at 57K; labor market in balance, Fed on hold through 2026
bullets.body: June nonfarm payrolls came in at 57K vs ~113K consensus, with prior months revised down 74K combined. The unemployment rate fell to 4.2% while participation dropped 0.3pp to 61.5%. Multiple desks (Morgan Stanley, Piper Sandler, Wolfe) expect the Fed to stay on hold through 2026; softer payrolls are seen as bullish for rate-sensitive names (consumer, biotech, housing) while reducing hawkish rate expectations that Morgan Stanley calls 'overdone.'

bullets.title: Fed Chair Warsh signals AI-era paradigm shift; inflation risks seen as coming down
bullets.body: Warsh describes the current moment as the most disruptive in modern U.S. economic history, calling for the Fed to rethink models, data, and balance sheet from first principles. He is viewed as signaling reduced inflation risks and a more balanced dual-mandate stance. Core PCE may be revised down from 3.4% to 3.2-3.3% in the BEA's September methodology update (software/portfolio management weight changes), potentially enabling earlier easing.

bullets.title: Macro backdrop: ISM Manufacturing 53.3, expansionary 6th month; prices fell 9.1 pts — largest drop since 2022
bullets.body: June ISM Manufacturing PMI hit 53.3 with New Orders at 56.0, both in their sixth consecutive expansionary month. The prices paid index fell 9.1 points to 73.0, the largest single-month drop since July 2022. This combined with OPEC+ adding 188K bpd in August (WTI ~$68.27) and softer payrolls supports the disinflationary narrative.

bullets.title: Hedge fund positioning: Info Tech net sold 4 consecutive weeks at -2.7 SDs; gross leverage at 85th-98th percentile
bullets.body: GS Prime reports Info Tech was the most net-sold sector globally for the fourth straight week (semis and hardware led), with US L/S net leverage falling to the 6th percentile one-year. JPM notes HF gross leverage peaked post-June expiry at 92nd percentile 12m / 98th percentile 5yr, with early de-grossing signs and July seasonality pointing to further reduction through late month. The momentum factor bottom requires: combined z-score of -1 to -2z, 2-3z HF de-grossing on 5d basis, and more decisive momentum selling.

bullets.title: Wolfe bullish on 2H26: economy, earnings, stocks; favors Tech/Semis, Industrials/AI, Healthcare/MedTech
bullets.body: Wolfe maintains a bullish 2H26 outlook across economy, earnings, and equities with Tech/Semis, Industrials/AI plays, and Healthcare/MedTech as three favorite sectors. They expect 2027 nominal GDP growth of 5.5-6% with 2% inflation implying 3.5-4% real growth, supported by monetary, fiscal, and deregulation tailwinds.

bullets.title: S&P 2Q EPS estimates up 3.4% during quarter vs historical -2-4% decline; broadening profit growth confirmed
bullets.body: S&P 500 Q2 EPS estimates rose 3.4% during the quarter vs historical average declines of 2-4%, driving 'earnings bubble' concern commentary. Nancy Lazar (Piper Sandler) notes non-tech profits have nearly doubled since pre-Covid, utilities and banks are benefiting from the AI boom, and Amazon Prime Day spending was up 9.3% YoY. Tech capex and AI investment are driving a productivity boom across the broader S&P.

bullets.title: Broadening trade re-emerging: rotation from semis/momentum toward hyperscalers, consumer, biotech, transports
bullets.body: Multiple desks flag the same trade: semis EPS revision breadth is at historical highs (peak signal), momentum crowding is unwinding, and the next leg involves hyperscalers, consumer discretionary, transports, and biotech. Morgan Stanley's weekly strategy note says biotech historically delivers ~20% annualized returns in falling rate regimes and the M&A cycle should accelerate. Oil decline benefits consumer discretionary and transports through lower rates path.

bullets.title: SK Hynix $28-29B Nasdaq IPO (SKHY) pricing July 9; Samsung Q2 preliminary results due Tuesday
bullets.body: SK Hynix is conducting a ~$28B ADS offering (177.9M shares, 100% primary) priced at ~$158.14/ADS with $7B in indicated institutional interest; pricing July 9, trading July 10. Samsung preliminary Q2 results Tuesday are expected to show ~18x YoY operating profit growth and ~130% revenue jump driven by AI memory demand.

bullets.title: Anthropic driving data center buildout: WULF 15.5%, IREN 7.5% pre-market on new capacity deals
bullets.body: Anthropic signed a lease at WULF's Justified Data Campus and WULF sold majority interest in Abernathy JV to Fluidstack. IREN surged 7.5% on reports Anthropic plans to buy 1.4GW of data center capacity in Australia. Separately, META is in final talks with Anthropic for Claude access in a reported $10B deal.

bullets.title: Broadcom-Apple extend custom ASIC collaboration through 2031; AVGO +4.5% pre-market
bullets.body: Broadcom and Apple signed new multi-year long-term agreements for Broadcom to develop and supply custom ASIC silicon for multiple generations of Apple products through 2031. AVGO expanded customer base beyond Google/Anthropic/Meta/OpenAI with two additional customers potentially including Apple per Jefferies.

bullets.title: MSFT PT cut to $525 on $270B FY27 capex and negative FCF; Azure growth raised to 41%
bullets.body: Wolfe lowered MSFT PT from $570 to $525 after raising FY27 capex estimates to $270B (from $230B) driven by memory price increases; FY27 FCF goes negative at -$17.4B vs prior +$14.7B estimate and gross margin falls to 63.1% vs consensus 66.6%. Azure growth forecast is raised to 41% for FY27 and 40% for FY28, and the stock trades at a 20% discount to Mega Cap peers at ~25x CY27 P/E.

bullets.title: Physical AI/humanoid robotics IPO catalyst: Agility Robotics SPAC drives sentiment around TSLA, MRVL
bullets.body: The Agility Robotics IPO via SPAC is spotlighting the Physical AI ecosystem. Humanoids are expected to impact supply chains and labor markets materially within 5+ years, with TSLA and MRVL positioned as platform plays. ARM's CEO separately noted CPU demand is 'off the charts' driven by agentic AI adoption.

bullets.title: June payroll softness bullish for rate-sensitive plays; biotech, housing, consumer discretionary flagged
bullets.body: With June payrolls at 57K and core PCE potentially revised down via BEA methodology changes in September, Piper Sandler and Morgan Stanley both highlight rate-sensitive sectors as near-term beneficiaries. SPX 2027 EPS now $397, and at 5% upside per 1pt multiple expansion the setup is constructive for non-tech longs. Citi remains positive on US equities, preferring QQQ, Banks, and Materials.

bullets.title: New York proposes one-year moratorium on new large data center permits; orbital data center economics debated
bullets.body: New York proposed a one-year pause on new large data center permits pending community impact review, flagged as a potential constraint on the AI infrastructure buildout. Separately, Jefferies hosted an expert call on orbital data center viability, with economics highly sensitive to launch costs and the core debate being whether value accrues to launch providers, infrastructure suppliers, or compute operators.

bullets.title: OpenAI pitching $100B ad revenue target by 2030; ChatGPT on ~900M weekly actives
bullets.body: OpenAI is pitching advertisers on ChatGPT with approximately 900M weekly active users, targeting $100B in ad revenue by 2030. Separately, META's Watermelon LLM has internally matched OpenAI's GPT-5.5 using an order of magnitude more compute than Avocado, implying sustained capex pressure, while Alibaba is prohibiting internal use of Claude Code.
